- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >1.0) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk aversion.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative — cap forecast peak at 1-2% below true peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3-5 consecutive forecast days are above true mean, reduce next forecast by 0.5–1.5% to align with historical volatility.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period (last 10–15 days) price movements — increase forecast tail end by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is rising.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +1.0 → -0.5 → +0.5), model often misreads momentum — apply smoothing filter to avoid abrupt direction changes.
